a: An image is the built, read-only package (code + dependencies + start command). A container is a running instance of an image; many containers can run from one image.

q: What goes into a Dockerfile for a model API?
a: A slim Python base, pinned requirements (same versions as training), the app code and model artefact, the exposed port and a start command (e.g. uvicorn). Load the model once at start-up; keep secrets out of the image.

q: Explain pod, deployment, service and HPA.
a: Pod: one or more containers running together. Deployment: keeps N identical pods running and does rolling updates. Service: stable address and load balancing to those pods. HPA: changes the number of pods based on a metric.

q: Why not autoscale an LLM server on CPU?
a: The work happens on the GPU; CPU can look idle while requests queue. Scale on queue length, requests in flight or time to first token (e.g. with KEDA).
Availability: if one pod or node fails (or during a rolling update), the other keeps serving.

q: What are readiness and liveness probes?
a: Readiness: is the pod ready to receive traffic (model loaded)? Liveness: is it still healthy, or should it be restarted? Without readiness probes, traffic hits pods still loading the model.
